Based on the search results, **the longest bridge in the world** - specifically the **Lake Pontchartrain Causeway** - **opened on August 30, 1956**.

Key facts about this bridge:
- It is located outside New Orleans, Louisiana
- Length: 24 miles (38 kilometers / 23.86 miles originally)
- It holds the record for being the **world's longest continuous bridge over water**
- A second parallel span was later completed in 1969 to handle growing traffic

The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway connects the urban area of New Orleans with communities on the north shore of Lake Pontchartrain, and remains the world's longest bridge of its kind today.

Overview Vocabulary
On August 30, 1956, the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway opened across Lake Pontchartrain, Louisiana. The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway is the longest continuous bridge over water in the world. The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway links the urban area of New Orleans, Louisiana, with the smaller communities on the north shore of Lake Pontchartrain. The roadway is 38 kilometers (24 miles) long, and supported by 9,500 concrete pilings. The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway benefitted residents on both sides of the bridge. People who worked in the city had their commute time reduced drastically. The bridge also increases business for retail stores and restaurants in towns on the north shore by allowing New Orleanians and tourists greater access.

## The Historic New Orleans Collection's Post
[August 31](https://www.facebook.com/THNOC/posts/pfbid02iUF528G4cA7Xo4zYtFe97FksRXQyApAEX3Z9Gtzak1bbPFhHkRyqUccmHXFxopgjl?__cft__[0]=AZgK4b_QfRHj7sF800yvp3z96FnVN3yJN8F1SXZyKVcgercwZ8MkLlHoaxpqrOqBSKdKYCPE1QeQKpBZpHP4joVWxEHYn93fa_qpPh4WnnJowW25rp3qyUsKEvlu-kKl4ps-bVtkvb9DakozRw152egfSXZbxadR&__tn__=%2CO%2CP-R) ·
70 years ago this week, on August 30, 1956, the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway opened its tollbooths to its first motorists, who paid one dollar to cross the 24-mile span between Mandeville and Metairie. The engineering marvel set a world record as the longest continuous bridge over water—a title it still holds today. At its midpoint, both shorelines disappear, leaving drivers surrounded by views of Lake Pontchartrain in every direction.
Before the causeway’s construction, drivers faced a lengthy drive around the lake or a slow ferry ride between the north and south shores. The new route substantially shortened that commute and fueled a population boom in St. Tammany Parish, then a largely rural area.
Since 1956, the toll has increased and a second span has been built to handle growing traffic, but both sides of the lake remain as connected as ever. These images and photographs from HNOC’s collections capture the bridge’s construction and opening, along with the lasting impact it has had on New Orleans.

Before the causeway’s construction, drivers faced a lengthy drive around the lake or a slow ferry ride between the north and south shores. The new route substantially shortened that commute and fueled a population boom in St. Tammany Parish, then a largely rural area.
Since 1956, the toll has increased and a second span has been built to handle growing traffic, but both sides of the lake remain as connected as ever. These images and photographs from HNOC’s collections capture the bridge’s construction and opening, along with the lasting impact it has had on New Orleans.

Overview Vocabulary
On August 30, 1956, the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway opened across Lake Pontchartrain, Louisiana. The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway is the longest continuous bridge over water in the world. The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway links the urban area of New Orleans, Louisiana, with the smaller communities on the north shore of Lake Pontchartrain. The roadway is 38 kilometers (24 miles) long, and supported by 9,500 concrete pilings. The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway benefitted residents on both sides of the bridge. People who worked in the city had their commute time reduced drastically. The bridge also increases business for retail stores and restaurants in towns on the north shore by allowing New Orleanians and tourists greater access.

Based on the search results, **the longest bridge in the world** - specifically the **Lake Pontchartrain Causeway** - **opened on August 30, 1956**.

Key facts about this bridge:
- It is located outside New Orleans, Louisiana
- Length: 24 miles (38 kilometers / 23.86 miles originally)
- It holds the record for being the **world's longest continuous bridge over water**
- A second parallel span was later completed in 1969 to handle growing traffic

The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway connects the urban area of New Orleans with communities on the north shore of Lake Pontchartrain, and remains the world's longest bridge of its kind today.
